newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market steady at $70 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market steady at $70 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Tuesday were active at $70.00 per cwt, steady with Monday and down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
About 15,000 head had sold by midday in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, bringing the week to date estimate close to 68,000, sources there said.
In Kansas, 17,600 head traded, which brought the week to date figure to 31,800, according to USDA.
The active sales so early in the week fueled ideas that beef demand was stronger than expected or that packers were short on supplies to fill beef orders booked weeks ago.

Beef sales at just ahead of midday Tuesday totaled 216 loads amid mixed prices. Beef cut-out values were quoted up $0.10 to $0.22 per cwt on choice cuts and down $0.12 to $0.21 for selects, according to USDA.
Choice values were reportedly supported by a large percentage of unfinished cattle on showlists, which resulted in more beef being graded select, cattle feeders said.
Prices Wednesday were seen steady in light trading, with much of this week's showlist seen bought by the end of Tuesday, sources said.
